In Aramaic, the language closest to Jesus’ daily speech, the concept of sin often carried the weight of “missing the mark”—not just breaking rules, but falling short of who you were created to be. And every time lust replaces love, something inside you drifts further from your design.
But this isn’t where your story ends.
Because grace enters where shame tries to finish you.
Romans 5:8 says, “But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not after you cleaned yourself up. Not after you stopped struggling.
While you were still in it.
That means your battle with lust doesn’t disqualify you—it reveals how desperately you need a Savior who doesn’t give up on you.
And His love is not like yours.
His love is relentless.
It doesn’t flicker when you fail. It doesn’t disappear when you fall. It doesn’t trade you for someone better.
It pursues.
It restores.
It rewrites.
That’s why this hits deeper than you expected, isn’t it?
Because you’ve felt the difference.

You’ve felt how empty lust leaves you.
You’ve felt how heavy guilt becomes.
You’ve felt how your spirit aches for something real.
And maybe… you’re tired of pretending you’re okay.
Be honest.
You’re not alone in this battle—but you do have to choose your direction.

Because the longer you feed lust, the harder love will feel.
But the more you surrender to Christ, the more love becomes who you are.
And someone you know needs to hear this too.
Not to expose them—but to remind them they’re not alone.
Because the next time temptation whispers, you’ll need to remember what’s actually at stake.
And if you’re serious about growing deeper, about breaking patterns, about becoming the man or woman God actually created you to be—stay close.
Not to sell you something—but to equip you.
Because this fight is real.
And you weren’t meant to fight it alone.
Here’s what you need to remember when the silence gets loud and temptation gets closer:
Lust will always feel easier… until you realize it’s slowly stealing your ability to love.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: How Could a Man Walk 120 Years With God… and Still Leave Us Wanting More?
paragraphs: How Could a Man Walk 120 Years With God… and Still Leave Us Wanting More?
The Number Wasn’t the Miracle… His Surrender Was.
Somewhere between the desert heat and the silence of Mount Nebo, there’s a question that doesn’t sit quietly.
How do we know Moses was about 120 years old?
And maybe more unsettling than that… what did those 120 years actually look like in the eyes of God?
Because if we’re honest, most of us aren’t afraid of dying early.
We’re afraid of living long… and wasting it.
Scripture doesn’t leave Moses’ age as a mystery or legend. It confronts us with it, directly, boldly, almost uncomfortably clear:

וּמֹשֶׁה בֶּן־מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה בְּמֹתוֹ לֹא־כָהֲתָה עֵינוֹ וְלֹא־נָס לֵחֹה׃
“Mosheh ben-me’ah ve’esrim shanah b’moto, lo-kahatah eino, velo-nas lechoh.”
“Now Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eye was not dim, nor his natural vigor diminished.” (Deuteronomy 34:7)
One hundred and twenty.
Not symbolic. Not exaggerated. Not poetic filler.
A number anchored in covenant history.
But here’s what grips the soul—Scripture doesn’t emphasize the number to impress us.
It reveals it to expose us.
Because Moses didn’t just live long.
He lived broken… then called… then resisted… then transformed… then surrendered.
And God counted every year.
Acts 7:23 whispers into that timeline:

Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦτο αὐτῷ τεσσεράκοντα ἔτη…
“When he was about forty years old…”
Forty years in Egypt.
Forty years in exile.
Forty years leading people who complained about miracles.
Three chapters of a life most people would have quit in the first paragraph.
But God didn’t waste a single season.
And neither did Moses—once he stopped running.
Because the scandal of Moses’ story isn’t that he lived to 120.
It’s that he wasn’t supposed to be the one God used.
A murderer.
A fugitive.
A man who said, “I am not eloquent.”

לֹא אִישׁ דְּבָרִים אָנֹכִי… כְּבַד־פֶּה וּכְבַד לָשׁוֹן אָנֹכִי
“Lo ish devarim anokhi… kevad-peh u’khevad lashon anokhi.”
“I am not a man of words… I am slow of speech and tongue.” (Exodus 4:10)
Yet somehow, this same man stood before Pharaoh, split seas, carried commandments, and walked so closely with God that Scripture says:

“וּמֹשֶׁה לֹא־יָדַע כִּי קָרַן עוֹר פָּנָיו”
“Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone.” (Exodus 34:29)
He didn’t even realize the glory was on him.
And maybe that’s the point.
The world measures years.
God measures surrender.
You can live 30 years and be finished in the Spirit…
Or live 120 and still be burning with purpose.
Moses didn’t die because he aged out.
He died because his assignment was complete.
Let that sit heavier than you expected.
Because some of us are praying for longer life…
While God is asking for deeper obedience.
And here’s where it turns personal.
You’ve been counting time.
God’s been counting moments of surrender.
You remember your failures.
God remembers your turning point.
You think your past disqualifies you.
Moses would disagree.
No… heaven would disagree.
Because Moses’ life doesn’t prove how long a man can live.
It proves how completely a broken man can be rewritten.
And if you feel like your timeline is messy… delayed… wasted…
Then you’re exactly where Moses was… before everything changed.
So be honest.
Not polished.
Not religious.
Honest.
Because silence is where shame survives.
But confession is where grace begins to breathe again.
And someone you know needs to read this.
Someone who thinks it’s too late.
Not randomly.
Specifically.
Because sharing this isn’t just content.
It’s calling.
And if your heart is serious about growing deeper in Jesus Christ, there’s more waiting for you than just posts.
Not to sell you something…
But to surround your life with reminders that you belong to Christ.
If this message stirred something in you, don’t ignore it.
Honor it.
Support it.
Because glorifying God isn’t passive.
It’s participation.
And this… this is one way you step into it.
Moses lived 120 years…
But eternity remembers him for one thing—
He finally said yes.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: 🚨 WHAT IF SOMEONE ASKED YOU TO PRAY FOR THEIR HEALING… RIGHT NOW?
paragraphs: 🚨 WHAT IF SOMEONE ASKED YOU TO PRAY FOR THEIR HEALING… RIGHT NOW?
Would you know what to pray?
Or would fear whisper:

“What if I say the wrong thing?”
“What if nothing happens?”
“Do I even have enough faith to pray for someone who is sick?”
Too many believers believe prayer for healing belongs only to pastors, elders, or people with some extraordinary spiritual gift.
But Scripture says:
📖 “Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him…” — James 5:14
You don't have to be the healer.
God is.
Your responsibility is to love, pray, believe, and entrust the outcome to Him.

HOW TO PRAY FOR HEALING FOR OTHERS
A Biblical Guide to Praying with Faith, Compassion, and Surrender to God
This isn't a book about hype.
It isn't about pretending every sickness will disappear instantly.
And it isn't about blaming suffering people when healing doesn't happen the way we expected.
This is about learning how to stand beside someone who is hurting and say:
“I may not have the power to heal you—but I know the One to whom we can pray.”
Inside this Gospel Warrior resource, you'll discover:
🔥 How to pray boldly for someone's healing without turning prayer into a formula
🔥 A simple ASK → LISTEN → PRAY → TRUST → LOVE pattern you can actually use
🔥 How Jesus responded to sick and suffering people with compassion
🔥 What praying “in Jesus' name” really means
🔥 How to pray when healing doesn't happen immediately
🔥 Why faith and medical care do not have to be enemies
🔥 What you should never say to someone who remains sick
🔥 Seven specific things you can pray over a suffering person
🔥 How to balance courageous faith with humble surrender to God's sovereignty
🔥 How physical healing ultimately points us toward the resurrection hope we have in Jesus Christ
⚔️ MOST PEOPLE VS. FEW PEOPLE
Most people say:
“I'll pray for you.”
Few stop and pray right now.
Most believers are comfortable praying for themselves.
Few intentionally become intercessors for others.
Most want God to perform a miracle.
Few are willing to keep loving, serving, encouraging, and praying when the answer is delayed.
Most want certainty before they pray.
Few understand that biblical faith says:
“God, I know You are able. I will ask boldly. And I will trust You with the outcome.”
Which believer are you becoming?
It's for people who want to live it.
Resources on prayer.
Repentance.
Faith.
Spiritual discipline.
Identity in Christ.
Renewing your mind.
Overcoming sin.
Healing and restoration.
Biblical discipleship.
And practical Christian living.

• Books
• T-shirts
• Mugs

• And more
Your support helps us keep creating resources designed to proclaim Christ, strengthen believers, encourage repentance, and spread the Word of God.
⚔️ THIS ISN'T JUST ABOUT GETTING ANOTHER BOOK.
It's about becoming the kind of believer who sees someone suffering and doesn't simply walk past.
The believer who prays.
The believer who serves.
The believer who points people toward Jesus.
The believer who helps carry the Gospel forward.
If you want to honor God by growing deeper in His Word and help support the continued spread of biblical resources—
Then do three things:
you remember:
You don't have to be the healer.

title: 🚨 YOU CAN LOOK SPIRITUAL AND STILL BE CONTROLLED BY YOUR FLESH.
paragraphs: 🚨 YOU CAN LOOK SPIRITUAL AND STILL BE CONTROLLED BY YOUR FLESH.
You can know Scripture.
You can attend church.
You can worship with your hands raised.
You can even talk about the Holy Spirit…
…and still explode in anger, live in anxiety, carry bitterness, struggle with lust, lose patience, or have almost no self-control.
That should confront us.
Because one of the clearest evidences of the Holy Spirit working in a believer isn't how spiritual we sound.
It's the fruit our lives produce.

🔥 UNDERSTANDING THE POWER OF THE FRUIT OF THE HOLY SPIRIT
And How to Activate It

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance...”
— Galatians 5:22–23 KJV
This book was created for believers who are tired of knowing what Christianity should look like without consistently seeing that transformation in everyday life.
Because knowing the nine fruits isn't enough.
God wants His Spirit to transform your character.
Not just on Sunday.
At home.
At work.
When you're offended.
When temptation hits.
When you're waiting.
When nobody recognizes you.
When life doesn't go your way.

This book walks through all nine expressions of the fruit of the Spirit and shows how Scripture calls us to abide in Christ, walk by the Spirit, renew our minds, repent of sin, obey God's Word, and stop feeding the desires of the flesh.
🔥 INSIDE, YOU'LL DISCOVER:

• How to cultivate LOVE when bitterness and offense are fighting for your heart
• How to protect JOY when circumstances disappoint you
• How to walk in PEACE when your mind is overwhelmed
• How God develops PATIENCE through pressure and waiting
